root_cause.text: In `xfs_attr3_leaf_add_work`, when the leaf entries array grows, only the freemap entry exactly at the old end was adjusted; other freemap entries that start within the newly claimed space (between the old and new end) were not updated, causing the freemap to overlap with the entries array and corrupting the `firstused` calculation, leading to an assertion failure and filesystem shutdown.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description shows a freemap with `base=388` (which lies between the old and new end of the entries array) that was not adjusted after adding multiple xattrs, causing the name area to start below the entries array end. The patch adds logic to adjust all freemap entries whose `base < new_end` and `size > 0`, not just those at the exact old end.

Other freemap entries that start within the newly claimed space (between the old and new end) are not updated, leading to a potential freemap overlap and corruption of 'firstused'. bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
xfs: add CRCs to attr leaf blocks

Signed-off-by: Dave Chinner <dchinner@redhat.com>
Reviewed-by: Ben Myers <bpm@sgi.com
bic_trace_step.reason: The loop at lines 1422-1427 only adjusts the freemap entry whose base exactly equals 'tmp' (the old end of the entries array). It does not handle other freemap entries that might have a base inside the newly claimed space (from tmp to tmp+sizeof(xfs_attr_leaf_entry_t)). This leaves those entries with a stale base, causing the freemap to overlap with the entries array and corrupting the 'firstused' calculation, which matches the root cause. The fix would require adjusting all freemap entries with base >= tmp, but that is absent here.
